newsitem.title: FRANCE: FIGURE SKATING-URMANOV CRASHES BUT STILL WINS GROUP.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-URMANOV CRASHES BUT STILL WINS GROUP.

text.p: Olympic champion Alexei Urmanov crashed to the ice attempting a quadruple jump but recovered to win his qualifying group as the European figure skating championships began at Bercy on Sunday.

The Russian, who has not captured a major championship title since his 1994 Olympic triumph in Lillehammer, completed six triples despite his fall on the quad toe loop as he won a narrow victory over Igor Pashkevitch of Azerbaijan.
Pashkevitch came second last year -- skating for Russia.
However, he was dropped for the subsequent world championships when Urmanov, who missed the European championships with injury, was restored to the team.
It weas a decision which, along with a number of other problems with Russian officials, led to him switching allegiance to Azerbaijan this season.
Another Russian, 16-year-old Alexei Yagudin, was third, also falling on an attempted quadruple.
The skaters performed their free programmes with 15 from each of two groups going through to the main event which begins on Wednesday and concludes on Thursday night.
Titleholder Viacheslav Zagorodniuk of Ukraine and Russia's former champion Ilya Kulik were skating later in the second group.
Steven Cousins, who lost his British title in November after a seven-year reign, beat his conqueror there, Northern Ireland's Neil Wilson.
The popular Cousins, who plunged from fifth to 18th after a disastrous free programme at last year's world championships, finished fifth in his group on Sunday with Wilson 10th.

Cousins must beat Wilson this week to fill Britain's only spot in the event at the world championships in Lausanne in March, which in turn will determine participation in next year's Winter Olympics in Japan.
Cousins began slowly and fell on a triple axel but completed four good triples. Wilson managed seven but five were flawed.

Women's qualifying is on Monday and includes France's five-times champion Surya Bonaly who was restored to the team on Saturday after being dropped for poor technique caused by an Achilles heel injury.
